scenario.name: Microsoft KB5005413, CERT-FR & CISA DFIR — MS-EFSRPC PetitPotam Coercion (Zeek dce_rpc) & NTLM Relay Forensics (EID 4624)
scenario.overview: Imagine a fortified courthouse whose encrypted-file clerk is required to inspect any document path mentioned by an outside caller. A trickster phones the clerk naming a fake folder sitting at the trickster own street booth; obediently, the courthouse chief courier marches straight out to the street booth flashing the courthouse master identity badge, while the trickster holds up a live mirror reflecting that exact badge straight into a neighboring notary office to mint a permanent master credential. In this scenario (T1187, Microsoft KB5005413, CERT-FR & CISA DFIR, MS-EFSRPC PetitPotam Coercion , Zeek dce_rpc & NTLM Relay Forensics , EID 4624) at 10.10.4, the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: mS-EFSRPC Bind Over \\pipe\\lsarpc, then coerced Machine Account Outbound SMB NTLMv2, then cross-Protocol NTLM Relay to HTTP/LDAP. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering MS-EFSRPC Bind Over \\pipe\\lsarpc, then Coerced Machine Account Outbound SMB NTLMv2, then Cross-Protocol NTLM Relay to HTTP/LDAP, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection pivots on Zeek Event 5145 correlated across the documented kill chain.

stages.title: Stage 1: MS-EFSRPC Bind Over \pipe\lsarpc & EfsRpcOpenFileRaw Coercion (Zeek dce_rpc.log & EventID 5145)
stages.subtitle: Credential Access (T1187 - Forced Authentication: MS-EFSRPC PetitPotam)
stages.description: Ringing the courthouse built-in encrypted-file service counter over an open office pipe, the trickster asks the clerk to open a raw file located at a street address owned by the trickster, forcing the courthouse to initiate an outgoing house call. The attacker binds to the MS-EFSRPC interface UUID c681d488-d850-11d0-8c52-00c04fd90f7e exposed on \pipe\lsarpc (or UUID df1941c5-fe89-4e79-bf10-463657acf44d on \pipe\efsrpc) on CORP-DC01 and invokes Opnum 0 (EfsRpcOpenFileRaw) passing a UNC path pointing back to the attacker IP (\\10.10.4.99\share\file). Zeek dce_rpc.log records endpoint="efsrpc" and operation="EfsRpcOpenFileRaw", while CORP-DC01 logs Security EventID 5145 on \\*\IPC$ RelativeTargetName=lsarpc (logged in Network Event 5145 with ZeekLogStream=dce_rpc.log + Security EventID 5145, NamedPipe=\pipe\lsarpc , or \pipe\efsrpc, RpcInterfaceUuid=c681d488-d850-11d0-8c52-00c04fd90f7e, CoercionOperation=EfsRpcOpenFileRaw , Opnum 0 so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes Zeek dce_rpc.log: named_pipe="lsarpc" uuid="c681d488-d850-11d0-8c52-00c04fd90f7e" operation="EfsRpcOpenFileRaw" (which Connects to the MS-EFSRPC named pipe , \pipe\lsarpc or \pipe\efsrpc on a remote server and invokes EfsRpcOpenFileRaw with an attacker-controlled UN so that abuses Active Directory Certificate Services , AD CS ESC1/ESC8 or NTLM relay coercion , T1187 during "MS-EFSRPC Bind Over \pipe\lsarpc & EfsRpcOpenFileRaw Coercion , Zeek dce_rpc.log & EventID 5145" to mint a valid X.509 client authentication certificate for a privileged domain identity and obtain a Kerberos TGT via PKINIT , EventID 4768). Next, the follow-up artifact Security EventID 5145: ShareName="\\*\IPC$" RelativeTargetName="lsarpc" runs (which Uploads a service binary , such as PSEXESVC.exe over SMB2/3 to the target's administrative \\<target>\ADMIN$ share , C:\Windows\, opens the \\<targ so that executes lateral movement with immediate NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM privileges on the remote host , T1187 during "MS-EFSRPC Bind Over \pipe\lsarpc & EfsRpcOpenFileRaw Coercion , Zeek dce_rpc.log & EventID 5145", leaving correlated forensic traces in Security EventID 5145, System EventID 7045, and Sysmon EventID 17/18). On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ Zeek dce_rpc: EfsRpcOpenFileRaw over \pipe\lsarpc (UUID c681d488-d850-11d0-8c52-00c04fd90f7e) / ⇠#1 RESP 5145) from Node ① (#1 Coercion & NTLM Relay Host) to Node ② (#2 Core Identity & VLAN Switch), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Relayed Target (LDAP / HTTP)).

The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: mS-EFSRPC Bind Over \\pipe\\lsarpc, then coerced Machine Account Outbound SMB NTLMv2, then cross-Protocol NTLM Relay to HTTP/LDAP. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering MS-EFSRPC Bind Over \\pipe\\lsarpc, then Coerced Machine Account Outbound SMB NTLMv2, then Cross-Protocol NTLM Relay to HTTP/LDAP, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection pivots on Zeek Event 5145 correlated across the documented kill chain.
briefing.diagramTopologySummary: The forensic topology spans Node ① (Coercion & NTLM Relay Host), Node ② (Zeek dce_rpc & SMB , :445), Node ③ (CORP-DC01 , \pipe\lsarpc), Node ④ (Runtime Process & Artifact Context), Node ⑤ (Relayed Target , LDAP / HTTP), and Node ⑥ (Zeek dce_rpc & EID 5145/4624) across 3 chronological steps (#1 to #3).

steps.plainTitle: MS-EFSRPC Bind Over \pipe\lsarpc & EfsRpcOpenFileRaw Coercion (Zeek dce_rpc.log & EventID 5145)
steps.storyAnalogy: Ringing the courthouse built-in encrypted-file service counter over an open office pipe, the trickster asks the clerk to open a raw file located at a street address owned by the trickster, forcing the courthouse to initiate an outgoing house call.
steps.simpleExplanation: The attacker binds to the MS-EFSRPC interface UUID c681d488-d850-11d0-8c52-00c04fd90f7e exposed on \pipe\lsarpc (or UUID df1941c5-fe89-4e79-bf10-463657acf44d on \pipe\efsrpc) on CORP-DC01 and invokes Opnum 0 (EfsRpcOpenFileRaw) passing a UNC path pointing back to the attacker IP (\\10.10.4.99\share\file). Zeek dce_rpc.log records endpoint="efsrpc" and operation="EfsRpcOpenFileRaw", while CORP-DC01 logs Security EventID 5145 on \\*\IPC$ RelativeTargetName=lsarpc (logged in Network Event 5145 with ZeekLogStream=dce_rpc.log + Security EventID 5145, NamedPipe=\pipe\lsarpc , or \pipe\efsrpc, RpcInterfaceUuid=c681d488-d850-11d0-8c52-00c04fd90f7e, CoercionOperation=EfsRpcOpenFileRaw , Opnum 0 so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact).
steps.howItWorksInPractice: Under the hood, the observed step executes Zeek dce_rpc.log: named_pipe="lsarpc" uuid="c681d488-d850-11d0-8c52-00c04fd90f7e" operation="EfsRpcOpenFileRaw" (which Connects to the MS-EFSRPC named pipe , \pipe\lsarpc or \pipe\efsrpc on a remote server and invokes EfsRpcOpenFileRaw with an attacker-controlled UN so that abuses Active Directory Certificate Services , AD CS ESC1/ESC8 or NTLM relay coercion , T1187 during "MS-EFSRPC Bind Over \pipe\lsarpc & EfsRpcOpenFileRaw Coercion , Zeek dce_rpc.log & EventID 5145" to mint a valid X.509 client authentication certificate for a privileged domain identity and obtain a Kerberos TGT via PKINIT , EventID 4768). Next, the follow-up artifact Security EventID 5145: ShareName="\\*\IPC$" RelativeTargetName="lsarpc" runs (which Uploads a service binary , such as PSEXESVC.exe over SMB2/3 to the target's administrative \\<target>\ADMIN$ share , C:\Windows\, opens the \\<targ so that executes lateral movement with immediate NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM privileges on the remote host , T1187 during "MS-EFSRPC Bind Over \pipe\lsarpc & EfsRpcOpenFileRaw Coercion , Zeek dce_rpc.log & EventID 5145", leaving correlated forensic traces in Security EventID 5145, System EventID 7045, and Sysmon EventID 17/18).
steps.diagramAlignment: On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 across the topology from Coercion & NTLM Relay Host and Zeek dce_rpc & SMB , :445 toward CORP-DC01 , \pipe\lsarpc and Zeek dce_rpc & EID 5145/4624.
steps.detectionAndEvidence: Documented in Network Event 5145 (recording ZeekLogStream=dce_rpc.log + Security EventID 5145, NamedPipe=\pipe\lsarpc , or \pipe\efsrpc, RpcInterfaceUuid=c681d488-d850-11d0-8c52-00c04fd90f7e, CoercionOperation=EfsRpcOpenFileRaw , Opnum 0 under T1187): Apply Microsoft KB5005413 recommendations: block unauthenticated RPC binds via Group Policy (RestrictUnauthenticatedRpcClients), apply RPC packet-privacy filters (netsh rpc filter) blocking UUID c681d488-d850-11d0-8c52-00c04fd90f7e, and monitor Zeek dce_rpc.log for EfsRpc* operations.

steps.plainTitle: Coerced Machine Account (CORP-DC01$) Outbound SMB NTLMv2 Callback to Attacker Listener
steps.storyAnalogy: Obeying the file-opening request immediately, the courthouse core engine dispatches its own official machine courier straight out to the trickster street booth and dutifully flashes its cryptographically signed courthouse badge to open the door.
steps.simpleExplanation: In response to EfsRpcOpenFileRaw, the NT kernel on CORP-DC01 (System PID 4) immediately initiates an outbound SMB TCP 445 connection from 10.10.0.10 to the attacker IP 10.10.4.99 authenticating as CORP\CORP-DC01$ via NTLMSSP. On CORP-DC01, Microsoft-Windows-NTLM/Operational logs EventID 8001 (Outgoing NTLM authentication traffic to remote server 10.10.4.99) (logged in WinEvent Event 8001 with LogChannel=Microsoft-Windows-NTLM/Operational, EventID=8001 , Outgoing NTLM Authentication Audit, CoercedAccount=CORP\CORP-DC01$ , Domain Controller Machine Account, DestinationTarget=cifs/10.10.4.99 , TCP 445 so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact).
steps.howItWorksInPractice: Under the hood, the observed step executes Microsoft-Windows-NTLM/Operational EventID 8001: Outgoing NTLM authentication to target "\\10.10.4.99" (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , Microsoft-Windows-NTLM/Operational EventID 8001: Outgoing NTLM authentication to target "\\1 so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1187 during "Coerced Machine Account , CORP-DC01$ Outbound SMB NTLMv2 Callback to Attacker Listener" , In response to EfsRpcOpenFileRaw, the NT kernel on CORP-DC01 , System PID 4 immediately initiates an outbound SMB TCP 445 connection from 10 while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). Next, the follow-up artifact Sysmon EventID 3: Image=System (PID 4) SourceIp=10.10.0.10 DestinationIp=10.10.4.99 DestinationPort=445 runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , Sysmon EventID 3: Image=System , PID 4 SourceIp=10.10.0.10 DestinationIp=10.10.4.99 Destinat so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1187 during "Coerced Machine Account , CORP-DC01$ Outbound SMB NTLMv2 Callback to Attacker Listener" , In response to EfsRpcOpenFileRaw, the NT kernel on CORP-DC01 , System PID 4 immediately initiates an outbound SMB TCP 445 connection from 10 while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution).
steps.diagramAlignment: On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 across the topology from Coercion & NTLM Relay Host and Zeek dce_rpc & SMB , :445 toward CORP-DC01 , \pipe\lsarpc and Zeek dce_rpc & EID 5145/4624.
steps.detectionAndEvidence: Documented in WinEvent Event 8001 (recording LogChannel=Microsoft-Windows-NTLM/Operational, EventID=8001 , Outgoing NTLM Authentication Audit, CoercedAccount=CORP\CORP-DC01$ , Domain Controller Machine Account, DestinationTarget=cifs/10.10.4.99 , TCP 445 under T1187): Enable the policy "Network security: Restrict NTLM: Outgoing NTLM traffic to remote servers" (Audit All or Deny All on Domain Controllers) to log EventID 8001 in Microsoft-Windows-NTLM/Operational and block outbound NTLM coercion.

steps.plainTitle: Cross-Protocol NTLM Relay to HTTP/LDAP & Anomalous EventID 4624 IpAddress Mismatch
steps.storyAnalogy: Instead of answering the courier themselves, the trickster holds up a real-time mirror that bounces every handshake phrase straight into a neighboring certificate notary office lacking tamper-proof channel seals, minting a Domain Controller badge while leaving an impossible address mismatch in the notary guestbook.
steps.simpleExplanation: The attacker relays the NTLMSSP_NEGOTIATE and NTLMSSP_AUTH messages from CORP-DC01$ to a secondary server (such as AD CS HTTP /certsrv/ or LDAP lacking channel binding/signing). On the relayed destination server, Security EventID 4624 logs a successful LogonType 3 (AuthenticationPackageName=NTLM, PackageName=NTLM V2) where TargetUserName="CORP-DC01$" (10.10.0.10) does not match IpAddress="10.10.4.99" (the attacker relay host) (logged in WinEvent Event 4624 with EventID=4624 , Relayed Network LogonType 3, RelayedIdentity=CORP\CORP-DC01$ , Expected IP 10.10.0.10, ActualSourceIp=10.10.4.99 , Attacker NTLM Relay Host, AuthenticationPackage=NTLM V2 , Missing EPA / Channel Binding so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact).
steps.howItWorksInPractice: Under the hood, the observed step executes Security EventID 4624: LogonType=3 AuthenticationPackageName=NTLM TargetUserName=CORP-DC01$ WorkstationName=CORP-DC01 IpAddress=10.10.4.99 (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , Security EventID 4624: LogonType=3 AuthenticationPackageName=NTLM TargetUserName=CORP-DC01$ so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1557.001 during "Cross-Protocol NTLM Relay to HTTP/LDAP & Anomalous EventID 4624 IpAddress Mismatch" , The attacker relays the NTLMSSP_NEGOTIATE and NTLMSSP_AUTH messages from CORP-DC01$ to a secondary server , such as AD CS HTTP /certsrv/ or LDAP lacking channel binding/signing while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). Next, the follow-up artifact SIEM Relay Signature: TargetUserName ends with "$" (Machine Account), AuthPackage="NTLM", and IpAddress != resolved DNS IP of TargetUserName runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , SIEM Relay Signature: TargetUserName ends with "$" , Machine Account, AuthPackage="NTLM", an so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1557.001 during "Cross-Protocol NTLM Relay to HTTP/LDAP & Anomalous EventID 4624 IpAddress Mismatch" , The attacker relays the NTLMSSP_NEGOTIATE and NTLMSSP_AUTH messages from CORP-DC01$ to a secondary server , such as AD CS HTTP /certsrv/ or LDAP lacking channel binding/signing while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution).
steps.diagramAlignment: On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 across the topology from Coercion & NTLM Relay Host and Zeek dce_rpc & SMB , :445 toward CORP-DC01 , \pipe\lsarpc and Zeek dce_rpc & EID 5145/4624.
steps.detectionAndEvidence: Documented in WinEvent Event 4624 (recording EventID=4624 , Relayed Network LogonType 3, RelayedIdentity=CORP\CORP-DC01$ , Expected IP 10.10.0.10, ActualSourceIp=10.10.4.99 , Attacker NTLM Relay Host, AuthenticationPackage=NTLM V2 , Missing EPA / Channel Binding under T1557.001): Enforce SMB Signing, LDAP Signing (Domain controller: LDAP server signing requirements = Require signing), LDAP Channel Binding (LdapEnforceChannelBinding=2), and Extended Protection for Authentication (EPA) on all IIS/ADCS endpoints.
